cards.explanation: The answer is False. Paul asks if they stumbled so as to fall beyond recovery, and his answer is “Certainly not!” (Romans 11:11). So Israel's stumble is not the end of the story. Anybody who has dropped a whole tray of cookies knows you can stumble and still get back to baking.

The answer is salvation. Paul says that because of their trespass, salvation has come to the Gentiles, the people outside Israel (Romans 11:11). That's good news for every Gentile listening today, friends. Salvation is the thing in the box here.

The word is jealous. Paul says salvation has come to the Gentiles to make Israel jealous (Romans 11:11). He comes back to it in verse 14, where he hopes to provoke his own people to jealousy (Romans 11:14). When Paul says a word twice in four verses, I'm writing it on my apron.

The answer is much greater riches. Paul says, “…how much greater riches will their fullness bring!” (Romans 11:12). He's stacking it up, friends. Their trespass means riches for the world, and their fullness means even more. I love a man whose math keeps going up.

The word is save. Paul hopes to provoke his own people to jealousy “…and save some of them.” (Romans 11:14). His hope isn't just to stir them up, bakers. He wants them saved. Good teachers always know where they're headed.

The answer is life from the dead. Paul asks, “…what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?” (Romans 11:15). He's already said their rejection is the reconciliation of the world. Then he asks what their acceptance will be, and this is his answer. That's a big finish.

The answer is that the whole batch is holy too. Paul says, “If the first part of the dough is holy, so is the whole batch…” (Romans 11:16). The first part and the whole batch go together. I've pressed a lot of dough in my day, friends, and I like how Paul used a bakery picture.

The answer is to boast over them. Paul tells the wild olive shoot, “…do not boast over those branches.” (Romans 11:18). Being grafted in is a gift, so there's nothing to brag about. If I strutted around the counter bragging about my stamping, the cookies would just laugh at me.

The answer is True. Paul says, “You do not support the root, but the root supports you.” (Romans 11:18). The wild shoot doesn't hold the tree up, friends. It's the other way around. Any branch that starts thinking it's carrying the trunk needs a little lie-down.
The word is faith. Paul says the natural branches were broken off because of unbelief, “…but you stand by faith.” (Romans 11:20). Unbelief on one side, faith on the other. Simple as that.

The answer is False, because Paul says the opposite. He writes, “…if God did not spare the natural branches, He will certainly not spare you either.” (Romans 11:21). It's a serious line, friends. No wonder he told them not to be arrogant.

The answer is His kindness and severity. Paul says, “Take notice, therefore, of the kindness and severity of God…” (Romans 11:22). Severity to those who fell, kindness to the grafted-in Gentiles. He wants everyone looking at both.

The answer is to continue in His kindness. Paul says there's kindness to the Gentiles “…if you continue in His kindness.” (Romans 11:22). That's his condition, bakers. He follows it right away with a warning, so he means it.

The answer is True. Paul writes, “And if they do not persist in unbelief, they will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.” (Romans 11:23). So the broken-off branches aren't out of the picture, friends. That ought to put a big smile under any mustache.

The answer is that they'll be grafted in more readily. Paul writes, “…how much more readily will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree!” (Romans 11:24). If a wild shoot can be grafted in, the natural ones belong there even more. It's their own tree, after all.
